coverage: WHAT I DID NOT GET TO. (1) src/renderer/state/classic-save.ts (262 lines) and canvas-save.ts/canvas-file.ts (465 lines) — I read only their call contracts from project-runtime.ts; the guarded-write mtime/conflict logic and the domain-clearing in classic-save are UNREVIEWED, and A1's shape (a flag cleared more broadly than the write) is worth checking there too. (2) classicLevelStore lines 745-1282 (the eight classic commands) I read for commit/dirty routing only — I did not verify the per-command validation arithmetic (chunk-cell packing, colind growth, block ceilings). (3) I did not run the vitest suite; every claim is from static tracing, and I did not drive the app under CDP, so A3/A4/A5 are traced-but-not-observed. (4) I did not audit the ~19 test files in state/__tests__ for the 'guards that assert nothing' pattern — I only spot-checked art-zoom-tier.test.ts (which is a real test but scoped to the store, which is why it misses A4). (5) editorStore's aeon command layer: I traced routing (focusedDocId/commandDocId/isZoneScopedCommand) but did not verify ZONE_SCOPED_COMMAND_TYPES against core/editing/history.ts's applyCommand, which its own comment says must be kept in step. (6) Stale-closure hunting was limited to the state/ and hooks/ layer plus the specific MapViewport/ClassicLevelViewport effects I cite; MapViewport (1500+ lines) and ComposerCanvas (700 lines) were NOT swept for stale captures — that is viewport-seat territory but the overlap is real. (7) I did not check whether A1 also applies to aeon chunkLibrary/bgLibrary adds (projectStore.addChunks/addBgToLibrary are explicitly outside history; whether buildAeonSavePlan persists them is unverified). (8) agent/agent-handler.ts and debug-hooks.ts were read only where they touch the stores I was auditing.
verified_clean: spriteStore multi-document model (spriteStore.ts:244-373): the park/unpark is written field-by-field on purpose so the compiler catches a forgotten SpriteDoc field, and every by-id accessor (spriteDocState / patchSpriteDoc / readSpriteSnapshot / writeSpriteSnapshot) handles the checked-out-vs-parked split symmetrically — I traced all four; none can misattribute an edit to the active document.

canvasStore per-document isolation (canvasStore.ts:363-370 patch, 522-530 closeCanvasDoc, 453-465 loadCanvasDoc): every document lives in `docs`, `patch` rebuilds the Map for one id, closing the active doc clears activeDocId rather than promoting a neighbour, and loadCanvasDoc THROWS rather than clobbering a dirty document. The record/dirty decision table in the header matches every setter I read.

canvasStore.openCanvasDoc clears the hub stack for a reused id (canvasStore.ts:438) — this is a real guard with a statable failure input (reopen a closed canvas id whose stack was materialised by any prior canvasHistory() read; without the clear one Ctrl+Z installs the previous incarnation's differently-sized pixel buffer).

DocumentHistoryHub prefix dispatch and disposal (core/editing/document-history.ts:29-63): longest-prefix-wins ordering is enforced by the sort at line 33; dispose() unsubscribes, clears and removes; clearAll() disposes every stack. UNTITLED_SPRITE_DOC_ID is 'doc:sprite:untitled' (tabs.ts:63), so it does match the 'doc:sprite:' factory — no unregistered-prefix throw.

classicLevelStore act-load safety: openAct's `loadToken` (classicLevelStore.ts:345,402,443) drops a superseded read, disposeStacksFor disposes BOTH the outgoing and incoming refs' stacks (line 356-357), and `fresh` resets exactly the per-act fields while leaving documented workflow preferences (composerTab, paintDivergeMode, tileClipboard) sticky. The dirty-discarding reload is gated by planLevelActivation's classic-confirm branch, and isSaveSuccess (tab-activation/level.ts:36) blocks the fall-through to openAct on a failed save.

classicLevelStore's two-document commit split: assertSingleDomain (line 582-596) genuinely throws on a cross-domain dirty patch, and requireClassicHistory (line 607-620) is a real instanceof check with a statable failure input (a stack built during classicProjectStore's 'opening' window is a BoundEditHistory and is rejected by name rather than blowing up as 'record is not a function').

The late-mount listener class is closed for the two shared hooks: use-attached-effect.ts:44-55 runs unconditionally every render and re-attaches on element identity change, and both use-anchored-zoom.ts:65 and use-hand-pan.ts:53 go through it. I scanned every ts/tsx under src/renderer for useEffect/useLayoutEffect with [] deps that touches a `*Ref.current`: only three hits, all benign (ChunkGrid.tsx:182 observes its own always-mounted button; ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:200 is a rAF cleanup; session-lifecycle.ts:127 is the persist subscription). The remaining element-level listeners in the tree are only those two hooks; everything else at addEventListener is window/document.

ResizeObserver hosts are not members of the late-mount class: composer-shared.tsx:194-206 takes the ELEMENT (callback ref into state) rather than a ref object, and ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:602-625 keys its effect on `status` so a conditionally-mounted canvas is re-measured.

Subscription hygiene: all five imperative store subscriptions (session-lifecycle.ts:135,136,190,197 and ClassicLevelViewport.tsx:210) return their unsubscribe from the effect. ClassicLevelViewport's viewStore subscription filters its own echo by exact equality against camRef, so there is no feedback loop.

classicObjectArtStore's cache lifecycle (classicObjectArtStore.ts:236-311): dir change wipes, refreshGen drops a superseded publish, one setSprites per refresh, and evictStale takes the SET of live epochs so the two clock families don't evict each other. ObjectSpriteCache dedups in-flight builds and caches failures.

canvas-constraints-cache.ts: single-entry cache keyed by buffer IDENTITY (sound because canvasStore.setPixels replaces the buffer wholesale and never mutates in place) plus origin BY VALUE; __constraintsScanCount is a real assertable seam.

Session persistence validation (core/shell/session-persistence.ts:16-87): tabs are zod-strict-parsed with Home re-injected and dangling activeId falling back; the workspace record is parsed per entry so one corrupt entry drops alone; a restored viewport goes through viewStore.setViewport (viewStore.ts:104-108), which clamps zoom to [0.125,8] and x/y to >=0, so a hand-edited payload cannot install an unreachable camera.

openEngine()/openProjectDir() (open-project.ts:21-44) really are the single answer — classic wins the tie consistently, and project-runtime's four savers all route through it, so a classic open cannot cause the stale resident aeon project to be written.

findings.title: Aeon Ctrl+S marks the WHOLE project clean while writing only the current act's sections
findings.claim: `editorStore.dirty` is a single project-wide flag set by every aeon command in every act, but `saveAeonProject` serializes only the CURRENT act's sections and then calls `markClean()` — so edits made in any other act are never written and the app reports itself fully saved.
findings.evidence: editorStore.ts:243 declares one `dirty: boolean` for the whole aeon project; executeCommand (editorStore.ts:396) and executeAmbientCommand (editorStore.ts:474) both call `markDirty()` regardless of which act the command targeted, and commands mutate `project.zones[].acts[].sections` in place (projectStore.ts:129 getActiveLevel hands the live section array to the history). An aeon act switch is a pure pointer move — tab-activation/level.ts:165 calls only `setCurrentAct(plan.zone, plan.act)`; there is no save, no reload, no per-act dirty bookkeeping. aeon-save.ts:24 then passes `currentZoneId, currentActId` into buildAeonSavePlan, and core/project/aeon/save.ts:51-62 resolves exactly ONE act and loops `act.sections` — only that act's `.tiles.bin` / `.collattr.bin` / `.objects.json` / `.rings.json` are pushed (the only project-wide loop, save.ts:136, writes zone TILESETS, not section data). aeon-save.ts:33 then calls `useEditorStore.getState().markClean()`. Failure scenario: open an aeon project with two acts; on act1 stamp chunks / move an object (dirty=true); click act2's tab; press Ctrl+S. buildAeonSavePlan writes act2's section files only; markClean() sets dirty=false. dirty-tabs.ts:41 (`if (s.aeonOpen) return s.aeonDirty`) drops the dot from every level tab, project-open-guard.ts:58 reads aeonDirty=false so opening another project proceeds with no confirm, and act1's edits are gone. The current-act restriction is not defensive either — save.ts:55 THROWS for a missing act, so it cannot have been intended as a per-act filter over a whole-project write.
findings.fix: Either make the save whole-project (iterate every zone/act that has resident edits before markClean), or make dirtiness per-document: track a dirty set keyed by the same `level:<zone>:<act>` / `zoneart:<zone>` doc ids the DocumentHistoryHub already uses, have executeCommand/executeAmbientCommand mark the doc they routed to (they already resolve it — editorStore.ts:389/467), and have saveAeonProject clear only the act it actually wrote. dirty-tabs.tsx's aeon branch then becomes per-tab instead of `return s.aeonDirty`.

verdict.reasoning: I independently traced every link and none breaks. (1) load.ts:317-335 loads EVERY act of EVERY zone into the resident S4Project, so all acts' sections are live in memory. (2) projectStore.ts:75 `setCurrentAct` is a pure pointer move — no reload, no per-act dirty state; tab-activation/level.ts:54,165 confirms the aeon branch does nothing else (its header comment even asserts act switches are "always safe" because the project is resident). (3) projectStore.ts:129-140 hands the LIVE `act.sections` array to the history and core/editing/history.ts:97-120 mutates `section.tileGrid.nametable` / `section.objects` in place, so act1's edits persist on the resident project after switching to act2. (4) editorStore.ts:242,298-299,396,474 — a single project-wide `dirty` flag that both executeCommand and executeAmbientCommand set regardless of target act. (5) project-runtime.ts:154-167 routes Ctrl+S (and Save All) on any aeon level tab to saveAeonProject; no other writer emits section files. (6) core/project/aeon/save.ts:51-62 resolves exactly ONE act (and THROWS on a missing one, so it is not a defensive filter) and loops only `act.sections`; the sole project-wide loop at save.ts:136 writes zone TILESETS, not section data. (7) aeon-save.ts:32 calls markClean() unconditionally. (8) Downstream is as claimed: dirty-tabs.ts:44 (`if (s.aeonOpen) return s.aeonDirty`) clears the dot on every aeon level tab, and shell/project-open-guard.ts:49,58 reads that same flag, so `planProjectOpen` returns 'proceed' and opening another project replaces the resident project with no confirm — act1's unwritten edits are gone. Triggering state: an aeon project.json with two acts in a zone; edit act1 (stamp tiles / move an object), click act2's tab, Ctrl+S (writes act2's section_*.tiles.bin etc. only, then dirty=false), then open another project or quit. NOTE: verification was read-only — the Bash tool died partway through and never recovered, so I could not run the existing vitest suites; every cited line was read directly.
verdict.severity_correction: Downgrade critical → high. The mechanism is real and the fix is warranted, but it is LATENT at this SHA: /home/volence/sonic_hacks/aeon/project.json — the only aeon project that exists (no games/*/project.json) — declares one zone with one act, and with a single act buildAeonSavePlan writes everything resident, so no user work is currently lost. "critical = silent loss of user work" requires a reachable losing state; here it requires a multi-act (or multi-zone) project.json that does not yet exist. Multi-act is clearly a designed configuration, not an accident (shell/tabs.ts:100 "a palette edit made from act 1 is undoable from act 2"; session-lifecycle.ts:47 emits a tab per act), so this flips to critical the moment a second act is authored. One link I could not verify because Bash was unusable: whether the Project Setup tab lets a user add an act from inside Aurora — if it does, the bug is one UI action from reachable and the critical rating would be defensible.

findings.title: artStore.open (the aeon composer document) is in no project-lifecycle teardown and no dirty guard — unsaved art is destroyed silently on project open
findings.claim: A new/unsaved composer document with painted pixels is dirty only on `artStore.open.dirty`, which `currentOpenDirtySnapshot()` does not read and `endDocumentSession()`/`resetProjectRuntime()` do not tear down — so opening another project neither asks nor warns, and the aeon open path then overwrites the document outright.
findings.evidence: A New Tile/Block/Chunk document is created with `chunkId: null, liveTileIndex: null` (art-facet.tsx:36-67). Painting it takes ComposerCanvas.tsx's doc-local branch (ComposerCanvas.tsx:255-261): `setPixels(doc, ...)` then `markOpenDirty()` only — NO command is executed, so editorStore.dirty stays false (contrast the chunk-doc branch, ComposerCanvas.tsx:242, which does executeCommand). The work therefore lives solely in `artStore.open` (artStore.ts:122). currentOpenDirtySnapshot (project-open-guard.ts:55-62) reads classicLevelStore.dirty, editorStore.dirty, anySpriteDocDirty(), dirtyCanvasDocIds() — I grepped project-open-guard.ts, dirty-snapshot.ts and project-runtime.ts for `artStore`: zero hits. So planProjectOpen returns `{kind:'proceed'}` and useProject.ts:17 proceeds with no dialog. endDocumentSession (project-open-guard.ts:88-91) closes sprite + canvas documents and not this one, despite its own docblock claiming 'The next document type is added here once'. resetProjectRuntime (project-runtime.ts:223-227) is the same. Failure scenario: aeon project A open, Art facet, New Chunk, paint for ten minutes (no Save clicked), File > Open aeon project B. No confirm appears; openAeonProject then calls `useArtStore.getState().openDocument({doc: docFromChunk(first), ...})` at aeon-open.ts:86, replacing the painted document — the pixels are unrecoverable. Corollary: on the aeon->classic path nothing replaces it, so the document survives into the new project, which falsifies ArtToolOptions.tsx:194's stated invariant '`open` is aeon's open document and is ALWAYS null under a classic open'.
findings.fix: Add `artDirty: useArtStore.getState().open?.dirty === true` to OpenDirtySnapshot/planProjectOpen (project-open-guard.ts:44/49) so the confirm fires, and add `useArtStore.getState().closeDocument()` to endDocumentSession (project-open-guard.ts:88) and resetProjectRuntime (project-runtime.ts:223) so the document dies with its project on every path. The 'discard' branch (line 165) needs the close too.

verdict.reasoning: Traced end-to-end and could not break any link. (1) art-facet.tsx (actual path src/renderer/workspace/facets/art-facet.tsx, not shell/) handleNewTile/Block/Chunk open a doc with liveTileIndex:null, chunkId:null. (2) ComposerCanvas.commitWrites (lines 194-263) falls past the live-tile branch (202) and the chunk branch (209) to the doc-local path at 258-261: adoptPaletteLineForEmptyCells + setPixels + markOpenDirty + bumpDoc, with NO executeCommand — so editorStore.dirty and the history hub never learn about the work. (3) composer-buffer.ts:17-41,115-120 confirms the strokes live in doc.localPixels, held solely by artStore.open, with no undo entry and no file. (4) project-open-guard.ts:55-62 snapshots only classicLevelStore.dirty, editorStore.dirty, anySpriteDocDirty(), dirtyCanvasDocIds(); I read the whole file and it never imports useArtStore. endDocumentSession (88-91) closes sprites + canvases only; project-runtime.ts:223-227 resetProjectRuntime is the same; session-lifecycle.ts:144 calls only resetProjectRuntime on a key change. (5) useProject.ts:17 gates solely on confirmProjectOpen, then aeon-open.ts:86 calls useArtStore.getState().openDocument({doc: docFromChunk(first)…}) — or closeDocument() at line 94 when the library is empty — destroying the painted doc either way. aeon-open.ts's own comment (lines 76-78) states the now-false premise: "nothing can be dirty one statement after the project was committed, so there is no discard to confirm". (6) The guard's test file src/renderer/shell/__tests__/project-open-guard.test.ts has a four-field CLEAN snapshot and zero art cases; its canvas describe-block documents the identical hole one document type earlier. Concrete trigger: aeon project A open → Art facet → "New…" → New Chunk → paint → File > Open project B: no dialog, no toast, pixels gone. Two evidence nits that do not change the verdict: the corollary's citation ArtToolOptions.tsx:194 is wrong (that line is `const pixelPerfect = useArtStore((s) => s.pixelPerfect);` — no such invariant comment exists in the file; the nearest relevant text is the caps docblock at 106-124), and the defect is broader than "new docs only" since the chunk branch at ComposerCanvas.tsx:246-251 also marks artStore-only dirt when strokes land on empty/local cells. Note: Bash was completely unusable in this session (even `echo hi` exited nonzero), so verification is by full reads of the cited files rather than grep/vitest; every relevant file was read in full, so no grep-only link is unverified.

findings.title: The transform grid is drawn on classic's Chunk/Block Paint tiers, which have no pendingAction consumer — the stale action fires on the next TileTab mount
findings.claim: `ClassicArtOptions` renders the shared option bar (with the transform grid enabled) for ALL THREE classic pixel tiers, but only TileTab consumes `artStore.pendingAction` — so a flip/rotate clicked on the Chunk or Block Paint surface does nothing, sits in the cross-engine slot, and then applies itself to whatever tile is selected the moment the user switches to the Tile tab.
findings.evidence: s1-facets.tsx:435-440: `if (!isClassicPixelTier(composerTab, chunkPaintMode, blockPaintMode)) return null; return <ArtToolOptions caps={CLASSIC_TILE_CAPS} />` — and level-presence.ts:59-64 returns true for tab==='tile', tab==='chunk' && chunkMode==='paint', and tab==='block' && blockMode==='paint'. CLASSIC_TILE_CAPS (ArtToolOptions.tsx:162) sets `transforms: 'fixed-square'`, and ArtToolOptions.tsx:248-256 renders TransformGrid with `disabled` computed only for the `'doc'` case — so under 'fixed-square' all seven buttons are live and `onAction={requestAction}` writes artStore.ts:124 `pendingAction`. I grepped every consumer of pendingAction: TileTab.tsx:291-301 and ComposerCanvas.tsx:530-567. ChunkTab.tsx and BlockTab.tsx contain no reference to it. ClassicComposerDock unmounts the inactive tab (`{tab === 'chunk' && <ChunkTab/>}`, per classicLevelStore.ts:222-231), so switching to Tile MOUNTS TileTab, whose effect (TileTab.tsx:292) fires immediately with the leftover string and calls `commitTileBytes(out.bytes, 'Transform')` — a real, dirty-marking classicEditTiles commit. Failure scenario: Chunk tab, Paint mode, click 'Rotate 90'; nothing happens; click the Tile tab; the tile at composerTileIndex (which openAct seeded, art the user never chose) is silently rotated and the tiles domain goes dirty. Given the measured block-tier sharing, that one tile can reach many blocks/chunks. TileTab.tsx:274-281 documents this exact hazard as the reason its `finally { clearAction() }` exists — the hole is that two of the three hosts drawing the button never clear it.
findings.fix: Either give ChunkTab/BlockTab the same consume-and-always-clear effect TileTab has (over their paint buffer, via classicPaintSurface), or make `transforms` false for the non-tile tiers — the cleanest form is to compute the caps from the active tier in ClassicArtOptions (s1-facets.tsx:435) rather than passing the one CLASSIC_TILE_CAPS constant. Belt-and-braces: have ClassicComposerDock's tab-change effect call `clearAction()` so no string can cross a tier boundary.

verdict.reasoning:
I tried to break the chain at every link and could not.

1. Host gate — `/home/volence/sonic_hacks/aurora/src/renderer/workspace/facets/s1-facets.tsx:434-440`: `ClassicArtOptions` returns `<ArtToolOptions caps={CLASSIC_TILE_CAPS} />` for any tier where `isClassicPixelTier(composerTab, chunkPaintMode, blockPaintMode)` is true. `level-presence.ts:59-63` returns true for `tab==='tile'`, `tab==='chunk' && chunkMode==='paint'`, and `tab==='block' && blockMode==='paint'`. It is wired into the real facet: `s1ArtFacet` (s1-facets.tsx:537-544) sets `ToolOptions: ClassicArtOptions`, and `LevelWorkspace.tsx:175` mounts it whenever `chrome.toolOptions && pixelToolsLive` — and `usePixelToolsLive` uses the *same* predicate, so on Chunk/Block Paint the bar is drawn, not suppressed.

2. Buttons are live — `ArtToolOptions.tsx:161-163` sets `transforms: 'fixed-square'`, and the render at 246-259 computes `disabled` only for `caps.transforms === 'doc'`. So all seven TransformGrid buttons are enabled and `onAction={requestAction}` writes `artStore.ts:124` `pendingAction`.

3. No consumer on two of the three hosts — I read ChunkTab.tsx and BlockTab.tsx in full: neither imports or reads `pendingAction` (they read `tool/selectedColor/mirror/dither/pixelPerfect/zoom` from artStore only; their write path is diffWrites → planSurfaceEdit → classicPaintSurface). `PixelViewport.tsx` and `PixelEditController` never touch any store. So the click is a no-op with the string left in the slot.

4. No clearer on the tier boundary — `ClassicComposerDock.tsx` (read in full) switches tabs with `{tab === 'chunk' && <ChunkTab/>}` etc. (lines 133-137, unmounting the inactive tab) and its only effects are `setArtTier(tab)` and the selection clamp; neither calls `clearAction()`. `artStore.setArtTier` (line 111) only sets `artTier`. `LevelWorkspace.tsx` (read in full) never touches artStore's action slot.

5. The stale action fires and writes — `TileTab.tsx:291-301`: `const pendingAction = useArtStore(s => s.pendingAction); useEffect(() => { if (!pendingAction) return; ... resolveTileTransform(buffer, pendingAction, selection, locked) ... }, [...])`. On mount `selection` is null and `buffer = tileToBuffer(doc.tiles, composerTileIndex)` (line 161), so `classic-tile-transform.ts:132` clamps the region to the whole 8x8 tile, rule B is satisfied for a square tile (rotate-90 passes), `tileBytesIfChanged` returns bytes for any non-symmetric tile, and `commitTileBytes(out.bytes,'Transform')` runs `classicEditTiles([{tileIndex: composerTileIndex, ...}])` (TileTab.tsx:248-256) — a real undoable, dirty-marking commit against a tile the user did not target.

Concrete trigger: open an S1 act → Art facet → Chunk tab → click the "Paint" chip → click ⇋ Flip horizontal in the option bar (nothing happens) → click the "Tile" tab. TileTab mounts, its effect fires with the leftover 'flip-h', and the tile named in the breadcrumb (composerTileIndex) is flipped and committed. Identical via Block tab + Paint. The only escapes are benign ones that still leave the feature dead: a locked/reserved tile toasts "view-only — transform refused", and a symmetric tile is a genuine no-op.

I found no guard, no alternate consumer, and no caller that prevents the bad value — the finding survives.

Severity: `high` is right, not theatrical, but the framing should be trimmed. Two of three paint tiers draw seven live controls that do nothing (broken main-path feature) and the deferred write lands on the wrong tile (wrong output). It is NOT critical: the misfire targets the tile the dock breadcrumb is already displaying, the result is visible the instant the Tile tab paints, and it is one Ctrl+Z away on the classic undo stack (classicEditTiles is a command), so "silent loss of user work" overstates it.

findings.title: openAeonProject writes its fitted composer zoom into whatever tier happens to be active — usually the tile tier
findings.claim: `setZoom(fitComposerZoom(...))` is called before any composer has mounted, so `artTier` is still its default `'tile'` (or a classic tier left over from the previous project); the chunk-fit zoom is written to that tier instead of `'composer'`, discarding the fit and leaving the tile editor at a chunk-sized zoom.
findings.evidence: artStore.ts:111-113: `setZoom: (zoom) => set((s) => ({ zoomByTier: { ...s.zoomByTier, [s.artTier]: clamp(zoom) } }))` — it writes the ACTIVE tier. artStore.ts:97 initialises `artTier: 'tile'`. The only writers of artTier are mount effects: ComposerCanvas.tsx:81 (`useEffect(() => setArtTier('composer'), [])`) and ClassicComposerDock.tsx:81. aeon-open.ts:85 runs inside the async open, before React has rendered the facet, so no composer has mounted yet. Failure scenario (cold boot): open an aeon project whose first non-blank chunk is 16x16 tiles; fitComposerZoom (core/art/chunk-pick.ts:64-68) returns floor(640/128)=5; setZoom(5) writes zoomByTier.tile=5. ComposerCanvas then mounts, sets artTier='composer', and selectArtZoom returns the untouched default 8 — the fit the comment at aeon-open.ts:82-84 exists to deliver never applies. Meanwhile the tile tier is left at 5 instead of 24; because artStore is a cross-engine singleton that no project switch resets, opening the s1 disasm next gives an 8px tile a 40px editor. This is the same defect class as the artStore.zoom fix in 2b38e0b, just at a call site the fix did not visit; the tier test (state/__tests__/art-zoom-tier.test.ts) exercises the store in isolation and never touches this path, so nothing catches it.
findings.fix: In aeon-open.ts, set the tier before the zoom: `useArtStore.getState().setArtTier('composer')` immediately ahead of line 85 (the composer's own mount effect then re-asserts the same value, so this is idempotent). Alternatively give setZoom an explicit tier parameter for callers that know their target, so a zoom can never be written to a surface the caller was not talking about.

findings.title: editorStore.selection / activeSectionIndex / marquee are never cleared on an aeon act switch — the inspector binds to a phantom object in the new act
findings.claim: `selection` carries `{sectionIndex, index}` and `activeSectionIndex` is a bare number, both resolved against whatever act is CURRENT; an aeon act switch changes only projectStore's zone/act, so after switching, the object inspector shows — and edits — the object sitting at those coordinates in the new act, which the user never selected.
findings.evidence: editorStore.ts:88/122/138 declare selection, activeSectionIndex and marquee as app-wide singletons keyed by section index. tab-activation/level.ts:165's 'aeon-switch' branch calls `useProjectStore.getState().setCurrentAct(plan.zone, plan.act)` and then only restores the viewport — it does not touch editorStore. I grepped every `setSelection(null)` / `setActiveSectionIndex` / `setMarquee(null)` call site: they are all MapViewport pointer handlers, SectionList/SectionGridNav clicks, the inspector's Deselect and the agent handler — none is wired to an act change, and no effect keys on currentActId. object-inspector-aeon.ts:185-188 then resolves `level?.sections[objSelection.sectionIndex]?.objects[objSelection.index]` against getActiveLevel() of the NEW act and returns a populated `selected`, and its commit guard (line 217-222) re-reads the same stale selection so the key comparison passes. Failure scenario: OJZ act1, click object #3 in section 2, switch to act2's tab; the inspector immediately shows act2/section2/object3 as selected and MapViewport draws its selection highlight (selection is in the render effect's deps, MapViewport.tsx:476); typing a new X commits `set-object` against that object. Same story for activeSectionIndex, which CollisionPalette.tsx:103/133 uses as the target of whole-section 'Clear collision' / 'Reset collision' commands.
findings.fix: Clear the per-act slice on act change — either in the aeon-switch branch of tab-activation/level.ts (setSelection(null), setMarquee(null), setActiveSectionIndex(0) alongside setCurrentAct), or by tagging the selection with the act it belongs to and treating a mismatch as no-selection. The second is more robust since the agent handler and debug-hooks also switch acts behind the tab strip (session-lifecycle.ts:20-26).

findings.title: toolStore is a dead duplicate of four artStore fields
findings.claim: `useToolStore` holds mirror / ditherPattern / ditherSecondary / pixelPerfect — the same four fields artStore already owns and every surface actually reads — and has zero importers anywhere in src.
findings.evidence: toolStore.ts:14 defines the store; artStore.ts:33-36 declares the identical four fields, and TileTab.tsx:174-179, ChunkTab.tsx:174-179, BlockTab.tsx and ArtToolOptions.tsx:183-195 all read them from artStore. `grep -rn toolStore src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` outside its own file returns nothing (exit 1). It is a loaded gun of exactly the shape this codebase has been bitten by: a future caller reaches for `useToolStore.setMirror` and the mirror silently stops reaching the pixel controller.

findings.title: The persisted per-tab workspace record is never pruned, so it grows without bound in localStorage
findings.claim: Tabs are pruned on restore via `restoredTabIsValid`, but the workspace record (facet + viewport, keyed by tab id) is seeded wholesale and re-serialized every change, so entries for closed/deleted/renamed tabs accumulate forever under each project key.
findings.evidence: session-lifecycle.ts:164 prunes the session (`loadStoredSession(..., isValid)`) but line 173 does `useWorkspaceStore.getState().seed(storedWorkspace)` with no filter; workspaceStore.ts:33-38 only ever spreads into `record` and never deletes; the persist subscription (session-lifecycle.ts:127-137) writes the whole record back on every session or workspace change. requestCloseTab does not remove the closed tab's record either. Concretely: a project where the user opens and closes 200 canvas tabs over a few months keeps 200 stale `doc:canvas:*` entries in the aurora.session.v1 payload, and saveStoredSession swallows the eventual quota error (session-storage.ts:53).
findings.fix: Prune the record alongside the session — filter `storedWorkspace` to the surviving tab ids before `seed()` (session-lifecycle.ts:173), and drop a tab's entry in requestCloseTab.

findings.title: useHistoryVersion re-subscribes to the history hub on every render
findings.claim: The `subscribe` argument to useSyncExternalStore is an inline arrow, so its identity changes every render and React tears down and re-registers the hub listener on each one.
findings.evidence: useHistoryVersion.ts:60-66 passes `(cb) => documentHistoryHub.onChange(cb)` directly, unlike its sibling useScopedHistoryVersion (line 76), which correctly wraps it in useCallback keyed on `key`. DocumentHistoryHub.onChange (core/editing/document-history.ts:74-77) pushes into an array and the returned unsubscribe rebuilds it with `filter` — so every render of every consumer (TabStrip, LevelWorkspace, SpriteDocHeader, the property/inspector ports) allocates a new closure and rebuilds the listener array. Not a leak (the unsubscribe does run) and not a correctness bug, but it is per-render array churn on a hook read by most of the chrome.
findings.fix: Hoist the subscriber to a module constant: `const subscribeAny = (cb: () => void) => documentHistoryHub.onChange(cb);` and pass that.
